body.name: compiled terminal-or-residual verification transition
body.construction:
Write \(\zeta\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{res}}\zeta'\) only after the compiler has either completed every task or produced the unique residual-ready task characterized by failure of the graphical predicates in the initial-token compiler. In the completed case, the accumulated rational circuit is inserted as the first projection candidate. In the failure case, the residual token stores the irreducible task, its exact kernels and constraints, the fixed finite projection library, and the fixed finite signed-row-swap library. A projection \(P/D\) passes exactly when every reduced factor of \(D\) has the constructed positivity-ledger factorization and
\[
 D\,t_{a,H}^N-P(o_H^N)=0\pmod{\mathcal J}.
\]
A contrast passes exactly when its two rational-affine primitive-coordinate maps lie in \(\mathcal I_H\) throughout their recorded rational box, have identical substitutions into \(o_H^N\), have a target difference of certified constant nonzero sign after substitution into \(t_{a,H}^N\), and satisfy all primitive-probability, admissible-cell, and exact-support sign tests. The transition emits the first passing candidate in encoded order, consumes the residual token, and halts. Candidate acceptance is not part of the definition of residual readiness.
